transcript:
Header: 2025-09-09 16:00 - POC Weekly Sync (45m)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Acme Product), Jordan Lee (Acme Eng), Samir Khan (Acme SRE)

Summary: quick review of pilot metrics, discussion of canary rollout strategy and cutover criteria, monitor/runbook ownership, and next steps for dry-run and final go-live.

[00:00] Alex Chen: okay um good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll run about 45 minutes today, main goal is finalize the canary/cutover plan, sa- also look at monitoring and runbooks, uh Priya will walk through the runbook draft.
[00:22] Maya Torres: thanks Alex, quick heads up execs want a one week notice before final cutover, and we're targeting production traffic switch on 2025-09-22, so todays sync is to align on owners.
[00:34] Priya Patel: cool, i'll share my screen in a sec, i put together a canary runbook, a/b split suggestions, and dashboards; note some of the metric names from our test harness are slightly different than your prod telemetry so there might be a mapping table.
[00:48] Jordan Lee: yeah mapping is important, our observability team uses New Relic for infra and datadog for app traces, grafana for cross-team dashboards, so if your dashboards link to prometheus, we'll need the prom metrics names.
[01:10] Priya Patel: got it, i've included both prom and datadog query examples, and a link to a read-only grafana dashboard - will send after this call.
[01:23] Samir Khan: quick question about kv cache and session affinity, when we do a canary split does Redwood maintain KV cache warm for the canary hosts or will the canary get cold cache?
[01:37] Priya Patel: good Q; Redwood runtime maintains per-host KV cache but during canary we recommend a warm-up phase where 10% of traffic is gradually targeted to the canary to populate caches, the runbook has a warm-up step 30-60 minutes, and metrics to watch: tail-latency P95/P99, token throughput, and cache hit ratio.
[02:05] Alex Chen: also note fallback policy, if latency increases beyond 30% or error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes, automatic fallback to previous model variant kicks in. we should confirm your tolerance.
[02:20] Maya Torres: 0.5% sounds tight for checkout traffic, our SLO is 99.95 availability, so for canary thresholds maybe 0.2% error rate is too strict? we should define both automated and manual thresholds.
[02:35] Jordan Lee: agree, let's have a two-tier threshold: automated rollback at 1% sustained 3 minutes, but alert to on-call at 0.3% so humans can decide.
[02:50] Priya Patel: i'm noting that, runbook will include both auto rollback and human-in-the-loop escalation steps.
[03:02] Alex Chen: ops/monitoring: Priya, you mentioned token-level cost dashboards in Redwood Console, can we get cost delta for the canary vs baseline?
[03:12] Priya Patel: yes, Console shows token breakdown by route/model, and CMU link in the runbook includes expected cost per 10k requests based on your prompt sizes, but small variance expected due to batching.
[03:25] Maya Torres: on security side we need confirmation of key management - our compliance folks require KMS integration and audit logs for inference payloads for 90 days.
[03:38] Alex Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; for hosted we'll need to confirm retention options. Priya, can you attach the SOC2 and KMS docs?
[03:50] Priya Patel: yes i will attach SOC 2 summary and our KMS integration guide; note if you want HSM-backed keys we have enterprise options through our security team.
[04:05] Samir Khan: also need RBAC and SSO for runbook execs, we don't want junior devs to kick cutover by mistake.
[04:15] Alex Chen: RBAC + SAML SSO is available for Redwood Console, and there are owner roles for rollout. we'll list the minimum required roles in the runbook.
[04:25] Priya Patel: moving on to cutover approach, suggested plan:
- Phase 0: Dry-run in staging with production-like traffic replay (2 hours)
- Phase 1: Canary 10% for 1 hour (warm-up 30m) -> evaluate metrics
- Phase 2: Ramp to 40% for 1 hour -> evaluate
- Phase 3: Ramp to 100% (or 50% then 100% depending on business)

[05:00] Jordan Lee: question, for A/B validation do we support deterministic routing so the same user sees variant A consistently? we need that for UX experiments.
[05:12] Priya Patel: yes we expose routing keys so you can route by user id or session id, that ensures sticky routing for A/B.
[05:22] Maya Torres: we also want an A/B fidelity check - i.e. if model outputs degrade for a user group, we want it flagged. can we run quality evals during canary?
[05:35] Priya Patel: absolutely, we can run live quality checks against a holdout prompt set, and output regression alerts in the Console tied to prompt sets. i'll include how to wire that up.
[05:48] Alex Chen: on rollback criteria, besides error and latency, we should include quality regressions (human review finds drop in accuracy > 5% on critical prompts) as manual rollback trigger.
[06:02] Samir Khan: from SRE perspective, what's the expected number of connections and concurrency per GPU for the model variant? we need to provision LB and autoscaling.
[06:15] Priya Patel: for your traffic profile (50 rps peak), recommended pool size is 4 gpus with continuous batching settings, but Dedicated config allows burst capacity, i'll share recommended instance types and autoscaling policy.
[06:30] Jordan Lee: can you put those numbers in the runbook, like expected p95 and token/s per GPU? that helps us size pre-provisioning.
[06:40] Priya Patel: yep included.
[06:44] [07:00] Alex Chen: quick check on compliance for pilot datasets - are we redacting PII before sending to Redwood?
[07:10] Maya Torres: yes products team will run a redaction pass, but we may need Redwood to confirm advisory on payload retention and re-identification risk.
[07:22] Priya Patel: will add guidance on payload retention, and options for on-request purge. for Private deployments we can honor shorter retention windows.
[07:32] Jordan Lee: can you also include a troubleshooting section for common errors: model mismatch, tokenization shenanigans, kv cache thrash, and out-of-memory spikes?
[07:44] Priya Patel: yep, section 6 in runbook covers OOM mitigation, slower startup, and recommended kernel knobs for quantized models. note sometimes transcripts say 'KV cache' as 'C V cache' in autotran scripts.
[08:00] Alex Chen: timeline sanity check: default plan is dry-run 2025-09-18, canary week 2025-09-22, final cutover 2025-09-26, does that align with your launch commitments?
[08:14] Maya Torres: target is 2025-09-26 for customer-facing launch, 09-22 is internal canary so yes that works if we get the dry-run scheduled this week.
[08:26] Jordan Lee: need to confirm blackout windows for upstream payments batch jobs - they run nightly 02:00-03:00, don't want cutover near that.
[08:36] Priya Patel: we'll put a recommended blackout window in runbook and ask for final confirmation.
[08:44] [09:00] Samir Khan: question about model variants and fallbacks: how are model variants stored and rolled back? can we pin a model digest in case of drift?
[09:12] Priya Patel: yes you can pin model version hashes, and Redwood Console supports rollbacks to pinned variants, we also have automatic fallback to last-known-good variant in case of failures.
[09:25] Alex Chen: ops, who is on call during the canary, need names and escalation path; Maya can own product side, Samir on infra, Redwood SE on support.
[09:36] Maya Torres: i'll confirm internal on-call roster post-call.
[09:40] Priya Patel: i'll add Redwood on-call contact and a high-priority slack channel for the pilot.
[09:46] Alex Chen: ok let's talk cutover checklist items quickly: pre-cutover smoke tests, DB migration safe points (if any), feature flags toggles, data retention checks, canary observers, cost estimate signoff, approvals.
[10:05] Jordan Lee: DB migrations not in scope for this pilot but feature flag toggles will be used. we will add a sign-off gate in the runbook for PM + SRE + Security.
[10:18] Priya Patel: also adding a rollback dry-run step so teams know how to trigger policy and validate fallback works.
[10:27] Alex Chen: excellent, final part: measurables for go/no-go. Priya?
[10:33] Priya Patel: primary metrics: P95 latency within 20% of baseline, error rate < 0.5% (or agreed thresholds per Jordan), token cost delta within budget +/-10%, and no critical quality regressions on golden prompt set. secondary: successful KV cache warm rate > 80% after warm-up.
[10:55] Maya Torres: sounds good, i will route for exec approval once we receive the runbook and dashboards.
[11:02] Alex Chen: recap of next steps: Priya to send full runbook + grafana links + SOC2/KMS docs by 09-12; Maya to confirm blackout windows and stakeholder list by 09-11; Jordan to provide traffic split plan and routing keys by 09-15; schedule 2-hour dry-run for 09-18.
[11:25] Jordan Lee: noted. one last thing, any baseline benchmark spreadsheets to share?
[11:31] Priya Patel: yes i'll attach a benchmark sheet with expected p95/p99 and cost per 10k reqs.
[11:38] Alex Chen: awesome thanks everyone, i'll send recording and minutes, see you next week.
[11:45] End of call

References/links mentioned: Redwood canary runbook (link), Grafana read-only dashboard (link), SOC2 summary (link), KMS integration guide (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link).

- Priya to share canary runbook, dashboards, SOC2/KMS docs (due 2025-09-12)
